chunks: And by this chain, he said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The most worthy of people with God and with His Messenger is the one who initiates the greeting of peace.'

key_terms.أَوْلَى: Most worthy, most deserving, closest — implies a superlative degree of proximity and merit before God
key_terms.السَّلَامُ: The Islamic greeting 'al-salam alaykum' (peace be upon you) — both a salutation and a prayer for the recipient's wellbeing
key_terms.بَدَأَ بِالسَّلَامِ: Initiated the greeting — the one who speaks first, acting without pride or expectation of a greeting in return

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about who is closest to God in terms of greeting?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted by Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) by the same chain as the preceding narrations, reports the Prophet Muhammad's teaching that the person who takes the initiative in giving the Islamic greeting of peace (al-salam alaykum) is the one most closely aligned with God and His Messenger. The hadith places the practice of greeting first — before wealth, status, or eloquence — as a mark of nearness to the divine. For early Muslim communities, initiating salam was an act of humility and spiritual courage, acknowledging another as a fellow believer deserving of peace.

en.hubeali: ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The closest of the people with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and with His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup> is the one who initiates the greeting (السَّلَامُ)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Through the same chain of narrators

it is narrated from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘A person who is closer to Allah and His Messenger is the one who initiates the offering of the greeting of peace.’”
